game.npc.leathersmith.default.name: Leathersmith

game.npc.tailor.default.name: Tailor

game.npc.artificer.default.name: Artificer

game.npc.villager.lumina.name: Mira
game.npc.villager.lumina.desc: A local woman who greets adventurers at Hydea's eastern gate. She keeps a close ear on news from the caves and the northern roads.
game.npc.villager.ceralith.name: Aldric
game.npc.villager.ceralith.desc: A weathered farmer tending the fields east of Royas. He knows everyone who comes through the highland passes.
game.npc.skill_master.lumina.name: Skill Master
game.npc.skill_master.lumina.desc: A seasoned master who can teach combat techniques to those willing to learn.

game.npc.miner.default.name: Mining Master

game.npc.alchemist.default.name: Alchemist

game.npc.cook.default.name: Cook
game.npc.cook.default.desc: Prepares hearty meals and teaches cooking to travelers.

monster.goblin.name: Goblin
monster.goblin.desc: A sneaky little creature hiding in the shadows.
monster.troll.name: Troll
monster.troll.desc: A big dumb brute with a club.
monster.wraith.name: Wraith
monster.wraith.desc: A dark ghostly figure, drifting silently.
monster.cave_bat.name: Cave Bat
monster.cave_bat.desc: A leathery-winged bat that nests deep in the cave tunnels, diving at anything that disturbs it.
monster.stone_imp.name: Stone Imp
monster.stone_imp.desc: A squat creature with rocky hide, fond of throwing pebbles and cackling at its own mischief.
monster.bone_crawler.name: Bone Crawler
monster.bone_crawler.desc: A skeletal remnant that drags itself along the cave floor on broken limbs, relentless and silent.
monster.thornhopper.name: Thornhopper
monster.thornhopper.desc: A large, spiny frog that ambushes its prey.
monster.river_raptor.name: River Raptor
monster.river_raptor.desc: A bird of prey that hunts unwary souls from the riverbank.
monster.maka_maka_scout.name: Maka Maka Scout
monster.maka_maka_scout.desc: A lizardman scout from the Maka Maka folk, searching for prey for the hunters.
monster.river_spirit.name: River Spirit
monster.river_spirit.desc: A powerful water spirit lurking near the river, waiting for unwary travellers.
monster.maka_maka_hunter.name: Maka Maka Hunter
monster.maka_maka_hunter.desc: A skilled lizardman hunter from the Maka Maka folk, at home in the Cera Valley.
monster.mossback_boar.name: Mossback Boar
monster.mossback_boar.desc: A thick-skinned boar with moss and fungus on its back.
monster.nightwalker.name: Nightwalker
monster.nightwalker.desc: A demonlike creature that moves like a living shadow.
monster.tomb_spider.name: Tomb Spider
monster.tomb_spider.desc: A gigantic spider with a mottled grey body.
monster.bodak.name: Bodak
monster.bodak.desc: A dark creature with a wraithlike silhouette.
monster.forest_spider.name: Forest Spider
monster.forest_spider.desc: A large green spider that hides in the bushes to ambush its prey.
monster.lich_hollow_crypt.name: Lich of the Hollow Crypt
monster.lich_hollow_crypt.desc: A powerful lich wrapped in a deeply purple, torn cloak.
monster.shadow_wolf.name: Shadow Wolf
monster.shadow_wolf.desc: A sleek predator with dark fur that seems to absorb light. Hunts in silence.
monster.withered_treant.name: Withered Treant
monster.withered_treant.desc: A gnarled ancient tree spirit twisted by blight. Its bark is blackened and its roots tear at the soil.
monster.bandit_marauder.name: Bandit Marauder
monster.bandit_marauder.desc: A hardened outlaw who raids the highland roads. Quick with a blade and quicker to run when outnumbered.
monster.plague_rat.name: Plague Rat
monster.plague_rat.desc: An oversized rodent bloated with disease. Its bite festers and its speed belies its bulk.
monster.dread_archer.name: Dread Archer
monster.dread_archer.desc: A spectral archer whose arrows leave trails of shadow. It strikes from range and vanishes before you reach it.
monster.hollow_knight.name: Hollow Knight
monster.hollow_knight.desc: An empty suit of armor animated by a curse. Heavy, relentless, and immune to fear.
monster.void_wraith.name: Void Wraith
monster.void_wraith.desc: A tear in reality given form. It drifts through walls and drains the life from anything it touches.
monster.storm_harpy.name: Storm Harpy
monster.storm_harpy.desc: A winged creature that rides lightning and shrieks loud enough to shatter stone. Unpredictable and lethal.
monster.elder_golem.name: Elder Golem
monster.elder_golem.desc: A colossal construct of stone and ancient runes. Slow, but each blow can shatter a boulder.
monster.crimson_drake.name: Crimson Drake
monster.crimson_drake.desc: A young dragon with crimson scales and a temper to match. Not a true dragon - but close enough to be terrifying.
monster.moss_creeper.name: Moss Creeper
monster.moss_creeper.desc: A squat creature wrapped in living moss and tangled vines. Slow to anger, slow to fall.
monster.giant_forest_beetle.name: Giant Forest Beetle
monster.giant_forest_beetle.desc: An armored insect the size of a cart wheel. Its shell deflects most strikes and its mandibles can snap a sword hilt.
monster.feral_dire_wolf.name: Feral Dire Wolf
monster.feral_dire_wolf.desc: A massive wolf long separated from any pack. Hunger has sharpened both its instincts and its cruelty.
monster.corrupted_stag.name: Corrupted Stag
monster.corrupted_stag.desc: A once-noble forest spirit wearing the body of a great stag. The blight has hollowed it out and filled it with rage.
monster.forest_witch.name: Forest Witch
monster.forest_witch.desc: An old woman long gone wild in the deep woods. She speaks to the trees and they listen. So do worse things.
room.luminacaves.entrance.desc: A reinforced shaft entrance cut into the Xaryre foothills north of Hydea. The city's main iron supply comes through here. Cold air drifts from the dark ahead; the smell of stone and ore is thick at the threshold.
room.luminacaves.chamber.echoes.desc: A chamber where sound behaves strangely — footsteps multiply, whispers carry from across the room. Iron seams run through every wall. The city mining company has been working this chamber for forty years; whatever unease the acoustics cause, the yield overrides it.
room.luminacaves.passage.dark.desc: The passage narrows to shoulder-width and the light from the entrance vanishes. The next chamber is visible only as a faint brightening in the distance. The walls are close enough to touch on both sides; the ore veins here run unbroken.
room.luminacaves.passage.abyss.desc: Glowing fungi have colonized this stretch of passage — their light is faint blue and cold. Beyond them, the tunnel drops into territory that the mining company officially does not send workers into. The air here tastes different: older.
room.luminacaves.chamber.hollowcrypt.des: The passage opens into a natural hollow that someone, long ago, shaped into something more deliberate. The walls have been worked — not by mining tools. A carved lintel still stands above a low doorway cut into the far wall. Whatever is beyond it is not part of the mine.
room.luminacaves.junction.desc: The tunnel splits here. One direction leads back toward the upper mine and daylight. The other descends toward a lower section the company's surveyors mapped and then quietly declined to develop. The cold from below is noticeably sharper.
room.luminacaves.chamber.deep.desc: The cave widens into a proper chamber, its ceiling swallowed by shadow. The mining company's survey marks stop at the entry to this room. Faintly glowing fungi cling to the walls and the air smells of damp stone and something older — older than the mine, older than Hydea itself.
room.luminacaves.chamber.ancient.desc: Ancient glyphs worn smooth by centuries of moisture cover every surface. Whatever was once kept or worshipped here is long gone — only bones remain. The stone-cutting method visible in the walls is not the same as the mine above; someone else was working this rock, long before iron was the reason anyone came down here.
room.crypt.portal.desc: A passage that is clearly not mining work — the stone here was cut with precision that modern tools cannot match, following angles and curves that suggest intention rather than extraction. The sound of something mechanical in the distance; pressure on old metal.
room.crypt.chapel.desc: A round room that rises to a dome. No natural light — but the room is not dark. Faint bioluminescent growth covers the dome in patterns too regular to be accidental. Whatever faith was practiced here predates any record in Xarra's archives.
room.crypt.chamber.east.desc: Alcoves line the eastern wall — originally housing something that was removed long before this place was found. The stonework is consistent with the highest-quality Myriac construction: old-kingdom period, before the First Dragon Wars. Someone of means and patience built this.
room.crypt.attrium.desc: A vast atrium with two rows of pillars carrying a vaulted ceiling that shouldn't stand by the engineering principles of the last eight hundred years. At the far end, a massive altar faces a stone figure so large it is difficult to understand as a single carved object — the proportions are not human.
room.crypt.chamber.west.desc: The western counterpart to the eastern chamber. The alcoves here are still occupied — not by their original contents, but by whatever moved in during the long silence. The stonework is more refined than the eastern side; if there was a hierarchy in this place, it belonged here.
room.lumina.center.desc: Hydea stands at the foot of the northern Xaryre, the Breswelc river audible from every corner of the city. The main square is lined with thick-walled stone buildings, their construction as much fortress as town. Traders from the lowlands haggle with mountain miners, and off-duty soldiers watch from doorways. The weight of what is happening to the west has reached even here.
room.lumina.north.desc: The northern gate of Hydea faces toward the Trevyre foothills. Beyond the walls, sawmills and logging camps stretch along the tree line. The smell of fresh-cut pine mixes with forge smoke. Miners return through here in the evenings, carrying iron from the foothills caves. The gate road leads north into the lower Trevyre range — a direction few travel without purpose.
room.lumina.east.desc: The eastern district of Hydea is where the Nuvmito trail begins — the old crossing path that links the city to the valley settlements across the northern Xaryre. Travellers heading east carry mountain goods and return with valley produce. A woodcutter's post marks the city's eastern boundary; beyond it, the foothills open onto the trail head.
room.hydea.west.desc: The western gate of Hydea opens toward the Plateau Pass. Old fortifications crowd the road here, built for a time when every caravan heading for Xarra needed guards and every return from the pass was counted.
room.hydea.mine_district.desc: The mine district sits at the northern edge of Hydea, just beyond the northern gate. The shaft entrance descends into the iron-bearing rock of the Xaryre foothills — the source of most of the city's iron trade. The company offices and ore-sorting sheds line the road. Past the district, the Trevyre foothills begin their climb.
room.ceralith.center.desc: Royas is barely a village — a dozen permanent households and the forge that defines it. The smoke from Taro Vaeres's smithy is the first thing you smell coming down the Nuvmito. A few villagers go about their day with the unhurried pace of people who have lived their whole lives between the same two peaks. The feeling here is different from anywhere else in Lura: something old, something alive, still present.
room.gerlyas.center.desc: Gerlyas is quieter than Royas — fewer people, fewer fires, fewer words spoken to strangers. The valley narrows here and the sun is gone by early afternoon. The inhabitants remember things the rest of the valley has quietly forgotten: the names of the peaks, the old protocols for approaching a dragon's mountain, the shape of a carved wing in the oldest stone in the village. No dragons have been seen here in longer than anyone can say. The stories remain.
room.gerlyas.crossroads.desc: A natural crossroads in the mountain terrain south of Gerlyas. North, the village lies just over a short rise. West, the Whispering Woods begin at the treeline. South, a rough path descends toward the Plateau Pass junction. This place has no name on any map — the locals call it the south fork, and leave it at that.
room.gerlyas.plateau.path.desc: The path from Gerlyas joins the Plateau Pass approach from the east. The terrain here is rocky and exposed; the Xaryre has its own weather in this southern section, different from the valley above. The Plateau Pass is audible before it is visible — wind through the canyon system creates a low, persistent sound that carries further than it should.
room.cera.farmland.desc: The Grelmito path runs along the valley's eastern face immediately south of Royas. Farmland terraces carved into the lower slopes give way to rougher country as the trail climbs south. A few isolated homesteads dot the hillside — farmers who chose distance from the village over ease of access.
room.cera.hill.desc: A bare rise where the trees thin and the sky opens. From this height you can see across the valley to where Royas lies in its hollow below the peaks. Further south the valley narrows toward Gerlyas. An old stone post here — too eroded to read any inscription — marks where the valley trail begins its descent toward the deeper reaches of the Grelmito.
room.grelmito.3.desc: The Grelmito path passes through a section of mountain hollow, the valley walls pressing close. Ancient pines line both sides. The path is older here ? pre-dating the village, pre-dating even the oldest stonework in Royas. The stone underfoot shows grooves worn by generations of feet that had no written record.
room.grelmito.4.desc: The valley narrows in this stretch and the path follows the contour of the eastern slope. The valley floor is not visible from here; the path winds between spurs of rock. Ravens circle above. The sense of isolation from both Royas and Gerlyas is complete.
room.grelmito.5.desc: A junction on the Grelmito where a path breaks east into the Whispering Woods. The forest begins immediately ? an abrupt transition from open valley to old-growth canopy. The main path continues south toward Gerlyas; the forest way is optional but those who know it say the woods connect south toward Gerlyas and toward the pass system beyond.
room.grelmito.6.desc: The Grelmito descends toward Gerlyas along the eastern valley wall. The air is notably colder here — the valley narrows further south and the sun reaches the floor for only a few hours each day. The sounds of the village are just ahead: the low voices, the smell of a fire kept deliberately small.
room.whisperingwoods.edge.desc: The Whispering Woods begin at the junction where the Grelmito path meets the forest edge. The transition is immediate — the valley disappears behind the treeline within a few steps. The old-growth canopy closes overhead and the temperature drops. The constant soft sound that names the forest is present here from the first step inside.
room.whisperingwoods.path.desc: The forest deepens. The characteristic sound that gives the woods their name is present here in full — wind through the high canopy, constant and low, just below articulate. The trees here are enormous, their trunks wider than two arm-spans. The path continues south through old-growth oak and pine.
room.whisperingwoods.crossroads.desc: The forest opens slightly and the eastern valley is visible through gaps in the canopy. Gerlyas lies to the east — the village is close enough to smell the cook fires on still evenings. The path continues south into the deeper forest toward the mountain terrain where the pass system begins.
room.whisperingwoods.hollow.desc: The southern end of the Whispering Woods. The canopy thins and the mountain terrain reasserts itself — exposed stone, shorter trees, open sky. A path leads east from here toward the junction south of Gerlyas, connecting to the route toward the Plateau Pass.
room.nuvmito.east.1.desc: The Nuvmito trail leaves Hydea's eastern gate and immediately begins crossing the upper Xaryre foothills. The city fades quickly behind rock and pine. The trail is narrow but well-worn — generations of foot traffic between Hydea and the valley settlements has kept it passable. The path rises as it moves east.
room.nuvmito.turn.desc: The Nuvmito crosses a minor ridge here and the trail turns south. The eastern valley is suddenly visible below — a long green slash between the ranges, with Royas somewhere at its center. The descent begins. The trail narrows as it finds the first switchbacks down the southern face.
room.nuvmito.south.1.desc: The trail drops steeply through switchbacks cut into the slope. Loose stone and exposed roots make the footing treacherous after rain. Below, the valley floor is closer but still far enough to feel remote. The peaks of the Xaryre press close on both sides.
room.nuvmito.south.2.desc: The gradient eases and the valley floor stretches ahead. The Xaryre peaks flank both sides of the path; ahead, the valley widens where Royas sits in its hollow. Pine gives way to mixed forest on the lower slopes. The sound of the Breswelc is just audible from somewhere to the west.
room.nuvmito.south.3.desc: The trail flattens as it reaches the valley floor. The smoke from Royas is visible ahead — probably Taro's forge, running before dawn as always. From here the village looks like a handful of stone houses set against the mountain wall, almost indistinguishable from the rock it was built from.
room.plateau.hydea_gate.desc: Just outside Hydea's western gate, the Plateau Pass begins its descent south toward Xarra. The fortifications of the gate tower overhead; below, the mountain road drops away into the first switchbacks. This is the formal start of the Plateau Pass — the military road that connects Hydea to the canyon city. A guard post checks travellers in both directions.
room.plateau.south.1.desc: The Plateau Pass descends from Hydea's southern gate into the first switchbacks of the mountain road. The city walls are still visible above as the path drops away. Cut stone and drainage channels — this road was built to last. Snow lingers in the northern shadows well into spring.
room.plateau.south.2.desc: The pass road continues south through open mountain terrain. The Breswelc valley runs below to the east; ahead, the Xaryre range rises in successive ridges. The wind is constant and cold. Stone distance markers in old Myriac script stand at regular intervals along the road.
room.plateau.south.3.desc: The Plateau Pass climbs toward its highest point before the canyon descent. Wind scours the exposed stone road. Looking north, Hydea is small against the mountain range behind it; looking south, the terrain begins to hint at the canyon geography ahead. The path levels briefly before the final descent.
room.plateau.south.4.desc: The Plateau Pass descends through a long section of switchbacks after the upper road levels off. The mountain slope falls steeply to the east; to the west, a ridge blocks the view of the lowlands. The road here is the most exposed section of the entire pass — wind and weather hit without shelter. The engineers who cut this road built low stone windbreaks along the western edge.
room.plateau.south.5.desc: A long straight section of the Plateau Pass where the terrain levels between two ridges. In both directions the road is visible for an unusual distance — rare on a mountain road. Wind-carved rock formations flank the way. The altitude is enough to make exertion feel slightly harder. The next section begins climbing again toward the high point.
room.plateau.junction.desc: A junction in the mountain road where the eastern valley path meets the Plateau Pass. North, the road climbs back toward Hydea. West, the pass begins its descent into the canyon approach toward Xarra. East, a path descends toward Gerlyas and the southern eastern valley. An old Myriac stone post marks the junction — its inscription nearly worn away, but the four-direction carving at its base is still clear.
room.sunstone.pass.desc: The Plateau Pass turns west here and enters the upper canyon approach. The walls of the Xaryre close in on both sides. Ahead, the gap between Tresa and Roruk begins to come into view — the same canyon opening that from the plateau looks impossibly narrow. The stone underfoot changes from cut mountain road to ancient canyon floor.
room.elor.plateau.desc: The canyon narrows to its final approach and the view of Xarra stops you in place. The city fills the gap between two enormous peaks — Tresa to the west, Roruk to the east. Stone terraces climb both canyon walls as far as the eye can follow. The oldest structures near the canyon floor show stonework no human mason could have cut — the foundations that dragons and the first peoples shaped together, three thousand years ago.
room.elorium.north.gate.desc: The northern gate of Xarra is built directly into the canyon wall — the arch has no keystone because the stone around it was not assembled but shaped. Dragon-craft, the old name says, though most who pass through don't look up. The gate ward keeps a record of who enters and exits; everyone coming down from the pass is noted.
room.elorium.north.district.desc: The northern district runs along the first terrace inside the gate. The buildings here are newer — rebuilt after the Tyriovan raids of eighty years ago — but they sit on foundations that predate the empire. Market stalls sell mountain goods: ore, cured meat, pine resin, craft tools. The canyon walls rise on both sides, narrowing the sky to a strip above.
room.elorium.north.smithy.desc: The smithy district sits in an alcove off the northern terrace, sheltered from the wind by the canyon wall. The forges here run on coal brought up from the Breswelc river valley. The Xaryre iron they work is harder than lowland ore — Taro Vaeres in Royas learned his craft from a master who trained here.
room.elorium.center.spellbound.desc: Spellbound Street is the oldest continuously occupied street in Lura — the scribes and enchanters here can trace their professional lineage back to the city's founding covenant. The shop fronts are narrow but deep, packed with scrolls, reagents, and tools. Above the doors, small carvings of dragon forms mark shops that carry stock the academies cannot legally sell elsewhere.
room.elorium.center.market.desc: The main market runs along the third terrace where the canyon widens enough to hold several hundred people at once. Traders from the lowlands mix with mountain suppliers. On clear days the sky between Tresa and Roruk is a narrow strip of blue directly overhead — bright, and impossibly far up.
room.elorium.center.desc: The administrative heart of the city, where the canyon floor is at its widest. The Guild Hall occupies the largest building, its walls carved with the names of the founding compact between dragon-kind and the peoples of the Xaryre. The inscriptions are in old Myriac that few can read today — but everyone knows what they mean.
room.elorium.center.cathedral.desc: The cathedral was not built by human hands alone — the vaulted ceiling shows the characteristic smooth curves of dragon-craft stonework, impossible to replicate with chisel and hammer alone. The healers who work here are the best in Lura, trained in methods that predate Tyriovan medicine by centuries.
room.elorium.center.academy.desc: The Academy of Xarra is the oldest school of magical and martial arts in Lura. The founding inscription above the entrance reads, in Myriac: 'What we build together endures.' The curriculum includes techniques developed in collaboration with dragons before the First Wars began — methods taught nowhere else in the kingdom.
room.elorium.east.gate.desc: The eastern gate stands closed. From beyond it, the sounds of conflict drift in — distant, but close enough that you can pick out individual shouts. A guard captain stands at the inner portcullis and does not look happy to see visitors coming this way.
room.elorium.east.district.desc: The eastern district faces the Roruk peak and catches shade for most of the afternoon. Despite that, it is one of the more prosperous parts of the city — the clergy compound and several academic buildings occupy the choice spots near the canyon floor, close to the Cathedral.
room.elorium.south.district.desc: The southern district climbs the lower slopes of the Roruk flank in dense, steep neighborhoods — narrow stairs connecting terrace to terrace, the stone smoothed by generations of foot traffic. The Cathedral tower is visible from every alley. This is where most of Xarra's permanent residents actually live.
room.elorium.south.manufacturers.desc: The production quarter handles the practical work that keeps Xarra running — ore processing, weapon finishing, armor repair, food stores. The workers here move quickly and talk little. Everyone in this district knows how many days of supply the city has; it is not a comfortable number.
room.elorium.palace.desc: The palace occupies the widest point of the Tresa flank — a compound of interlocking courts and halls that grew over three thousand years from the original covenant-hall where dragon and human leaders first met as equals. The garden between the outer walls and the main hall is famous: plants from every region of Lura, kept alive through winters that would kill them anywhere else.
item.merchant_seal.desc: Deposit into your shop's storage to keep it open in its room even while you're elsewhere - as long as it stays there. A small fee is taken from sales made while you're not physically present.

npc.healer_default.dialog: Your wounds won't mend themselves. Let me take a look — a little healing and you'll be back on your feet.
npc.action.heal.ok: There — good as new. Come back anytime you need mending.
npc.smith_default.dialog: Come to browse the forge's finest? I've got steel enough to outfit a whole war band. Name what you need.
npc.leathersmith_default.dialog: Light armor, fast hands — that's the way to stay alive out there. I work hides and pelts into gear that won't slow you down.
npc.tailor_default.dialog: Cloth and thread are mightier than most give credit for. A well-sewn robe channels power like nothing else. What are you after?
npc.artificer_default.dialog: Rings, bands, trinkets — the small things that make the difference between life and death. I craft pieces that actually matter.
npc.enchanter_default.dialog: Magic lives in the wood and the binding, not just the wielder. My staves and tomes will serve a mage well.
npc.trader_default.dialog: Got something to sell or something to buy? Either way, you've come to the right place.
npc.villager_default.dialog: Not much to say, really. Just passing through?
npc.villager_lumina.dialog: Adventurer! Glad you're passing through. There's no shortage of trouble around Hydea right now.
npc.villager_ceralith.dialog: Good to see a traveler who made it through the highland passes in one piece. Things have been rough on those roads lately.
npc.skill_master_lumina.dialog: Class mastery is a journey, not a destination. Come to me when you're ready to change your path or sharpen your focus.
npc.miner_master.dialog: The veins beneath this city never run dry if you know where to look. I can teach you the trade — and sell you the tools to get started.
npc.woodcutter_master.dialog: Every plank in this town came from trees my students felled. The forest gives well if you know how to ask it. I can teach you the craft.
npc.herbalist_master.dialog: The land provides everything we need, if you know how to look for it. I can teach you what grows where — and how to use it.
npc.alchemist_master.dialog: Fire and water, root and stone — the right combination changes everything. Alchemy is the art of knowing which ingredients bend the world to your will.
npc.cook_master.dialog: A good meal is worth more than most swords. I can teach you to feed yourself — and fight better for it.

quest.co1_first_day.name: First Day in Hydea
quest.co1_first_day.desc: You have arrived in Hydea as a blacksmith apprentice. Speak with Gorhen the smith and get your bearings.
quest.co1_first_day.accept.1: Welcome to Hydea. You must be the apprentice Vann hired by letter — I am Gorhen, the town smith. You look like you have been on the road for three days.
quest.co1_first_day.accept.2: Three days, and the waypost markers ran out two hours north of here. Your roads are not well marked.
quest.co1_first_day.accept.3: They rarely are out this way. Here — a pickaxe and a mace. The pickaxe lets you chip iron ore from the cave deposits nearby; we always need it at the forge. The mace is for your own safety. Things near the caves have been restless lately.
quest.co1_first_day.accept.4: Understood. What do you need me to do first?
quest.co1_first_day.accept.5: Get your bearings. Walk the town, speak to the folk here. Mira in the town square knows everyone and everything worth knowing. Come back to me once you have found your feet — I have real work for you soon enough.
quest.co1_first_day.return.1: Good — you have had a look around. Now the proper work begins.
quest.co1_gather_ore.name: The Forge Never Rests
quest.co1_gather_ore.desc: Gorhen the smith needs iron ore to keep the forge running. Head into the cave to the south and gather four lumps of iron ore using your pickaxe.
quest.co1_gather_ore.accept.1: Good timing. My ore stock is nearly gone and I have three orders to fill before the week is out. I need iron ore from the cave deposits to the south.
quest.co1_gather_ore.accept.3: Four chunks will do for now. Take your pickaxe and head into the cave entrance. Look for the shimmering walls — those are the ore veins. Strike them and gather what falls. The outer tunnels are safe enough. Mind the bats if you wander deeper.
quest.co1_gather_ore.return.1: Four good lumps of ore — and clean breaks too. You have a steady hand with a pickaxe. This is enough to keep the forge burning through the week. Here, for your trouble.
quest.co1_first_ironwork.name: Hands on the Anvil
quest.co1_first_ironwork.desc: Gorhen wants to see if you can work the forge. Smelt an iron ingot using the Craft option at the forge — two iron ore makes one ingot — then bring it back to him.
quest.co1_first_ironwork.accept.1: Now that we have ore, it is time you learned the forge. You cannot call yourself a smith's apprentice without knowing how to smelt.
quest.co1_first_ironwork.accept.2: I have used forges before, but never for fine work.
quest.co1_first_ironwork.accept.3: Then you already know the hard part. Two pieces of ore in the furnace makes one iron ingot. Speak to me and look for the Craft option — I will guide you through the furnace. Bring me one clean ingot and we will call this lesson done.
quest.co1_first_ironwork.return.1: An iron ingot, clean and solid — no slag, no cracking. Better than most first attempts I have seen. You have real hands for this trade. Keep it up and you will be smelting chain links by the end of the month. Here is your cut.
quest.co1_goblins.name: Something Wicked at the South Gate
quest.co1_goblins.desc: Mira, the town's unofficial voice, has spotted goblins creeping closer to the road. Put down three of them to drive the rest back.
quest.co1_goblins.accept.1: You must be Gorhen's new apprentice! I am Mira — I help keep things organized around town, for all the good it does these days. I have been looking for you.
quest.co1_goblins.accept.2: Looking for me? We have not met before.
quest.co1_goblins.accept.3: Word travels fast in a small town. And right now that word is goblins. They have been skulking closer and closer to the south road all week. One nearly spooked old Harev's horse into a ditch yesterday. I see you have a mace at your belt — could you deal with three of them? Just enough to push the rest back from the road.
quest.co1_goblins.accept.4: Three goblins. Manageable. I will handle it.
quest.co1_goblins.accept.5: Head for the cave entrance south of the market — they have been scouting near there. Be careful; goblins are quick. Hit first and keep moving.
quest.co1_goblins.return.1: Three goblins! The road watch said they scattered before sunset — you must have hit them right where it hurt. You fight well for a smith's apprentice. Here, this comes from the town's emergency fund. You have more than earned it.
quest.co1_skill_intro.name: The Training Hall
quest.co1_skill_intro.desc: Mira wants you to meet Edric, the town's class master, who can teach you proper combat techniques. Speak to him at the training hall east of the square.
quest.co1_skill_intro.accept.1: You handled those goblins well, but you will face tougher things the deeper you go into those caves. Have you spoken with Edric yet?
quest.co1_skill_intro.accept.2: I have not. Who is he?
quest.co1_skill_intro.accept.3: Our class master. He trains fighters, mages, and everything in between. Real techniques, not just swinging until something falls over. He is at the training hall, just east of the square. Tell him I sent you — he is more likely to take you seriously that way.
quest.co1_skill_intro.return.1: Mira sent you? Good — sit down. Combat is not just about hitting hard. It is about knowing when and how to strike.
quest.co1_skill_intro.return.2: I have been getting by on instinct.
quest.co1_skill_intro.return.3: Instinct keeps you alive on a good day. Skills keep you alive every day. Open your Skills menu and look at what is available to you — each one can be assigned to a combat slot and used in battle. Once you have more experience, come back. I can train you further. For now, you are ready for what the road will throw at you.
quest.co1_troll.name: The Blockade
quest.co1_troll.desc: A troll has taken up residence in the main cave passage and is blocking the miners from the deeper veins. Mira is asking you to drive it out.
quest.co1_troll.accept.1: I have been putting off telling anyone about this, but I cannot wait any longer. There is a troll. It took up residence just inside the main cave passage three days ago and has blocked the miners from reaching the deeper ore veins entirely.
quest.co1_troll.accept.2: A troll. That is not the same as three goblins.
quest.co1_troll.accept.3: No. It is not. But after what you did at the south road — and with Edric's teaching behind you now — I believe you can manage it. The miners need those veins, and I will not ask someone weaker to take that risk when you are standing right here.
quest.co1_troll.accept.5: Be careful. Trolls hit hard and they do not stop until they are down. Use every skill you have. And come back in one piece — Gorhen would never let me hear the end of it otherwise.
quest.co1_troll.return.1: The miners came back an hour ago singing your name. A troll — by yourself! I knew you could do it, but I still held my breath until I heard. This town owes you more than a handful of gold, but it is a start.
quest.co1_trusted.name: Part of the Town
quest.co1_trusted.desc: Gorhen has heard of your deeds and wants to speak with you. Return to the forge.
quest.co1_trusted.accept.1: Word travels fast in a small town. A troll in the main passage — alone. Mira is already calling you the town's protector.
quest.co1_trusted.accept.2: I just did what needed doing.
quest.co1_trusted.accept.3: That is exactly what a protector says. Listen — you came here as my apprentice, and that is still true. But you are more than that now. I have been holding this armor back for the right person.
quest.co1_trusted.accept.4: You are part of Hydea now. Smith by trade, defender by deed. The road ahead will throw harder things at you than trolls and goblins — it always does out here. But I think you are ready for it.
quest.co1_trusted.return.1: The armor suits you. Good. There is always more work ahead in a town like this — but at least now we face it together.
quest.forest_infestation.name: Something in the Undergrowth
quest.forest_infestation.desc: Moss Creepers have been spreading out of the Whispering Woods and tearing up the road edges east of Hydea. Clear eight of them before the damage reaches the town gate.
quest.forest_infestation.accept.1: Something has been tearing at the road edges east of town. Not goblins — slower, but stubborn. The foresters are calling them Moss Creepers. They come out of the Whispering Woods.
quest.forest_infestation.accept.3: Plant things. Wrapped in vine and moss, not much smarter than a badger, but they do not stop once they start digging. Eight of them are working on the eastern embankment right now. If they reach the stone foundations we will have a real problem.
quest.forest_infestation.return.1: The road crew went out at dawn and came back relieved. No more digging overnight. You got to them before any real damage was done — here is what was promised.
quest.beetle_problem.name: Armored and Angry
quest.beetle_problem.desc: Giant Forest Beetles have taken over a section of the woodcutters' trail. The lumber operation is stalled until they are cleared.
quest.beetle_problem.accept.1: The woodcutters are backed up again. Giant Forest Beetles — six or more of them — have claimed the main trail. The lumberjacks tried to push through and two of them came back without their equipment.
quest.beetle_problem.accept.2: Their shells are the issue. Hard to crack.
quest.beetle_problem.accept.3: Hit the joints, not the back. That is what old Harev's grandfather used to say, anyway. Six beetles and the trail opens again. The whole town's wood supply depends on it.
quest.beetle_problem.return.1: The woodcutters sent word an hour ago — trail is clear and they are already back to work. I found one of their tools in the undergrowth too; looks like the beetles had been sitting on it for days. Here is your reward.
quest.dire_wolves.name: Pack Mentality
quest.dire_wolves.desc: Feral Dire Wolves have been trailing the forest patrols and ambushing stragglers. Drive back ten of them.
quest.dire_wolves.accept.1: We have lost two patrol rangers to wolf attacks this month. Not cave wolves — something bigger, meaner. The trackers found prints twice the size of a normal wolf. They are calling them Dire Wolves.
quest.dire_wolves.accept.3: Lone, but they have been trailing each other — same territory. Ten encounters should be enough to push the survivors deep enough into the woods that the patrols are safe again. Watch your flanks; they come from the side, not the front.
quest.dire_wolves.return.1: The patrol completed a full circuit this morning without incident. Whatever was hunting them has pulled back. You have given those rangers their confidence back — and this town its forest back too. Here.
quest.corrupted_heart.name: The Forest's Grief
quest.corrupted_heart.desc: Something is wrong at the heart of the Whispering Woods. Corrupted Stags — spirits eaten hollow by the blight — are driving everything else out. Put four of them to rest.
quest.corrupted_heart.accept.1: A herbalist came to me last night, shaken. She said she saw a stag the size of a horse at the forest hollow — its eyes were wrong, like looking into something that had already died but not stopped moving.
quest.corrupted_heart.accept.2: Corrupted spirits. The blight has reached the older creatures.
quest.corrupted_heart.accept.3: They were guardians once, or so the old stories say. Now they are just pain given legs. Four of them have been seen. End them — it is mercy as much as necessity. The hollow cannot heal while they are still there.
quest.corrupted_heart.return.1: The herbalist went back at dawn. She said the hollow felt lighter — her words. I do not know what that means exactly, but I know what you did made it possible. Thank you. Here is your reward.
quest.witch_coven.name: The Coven in the Deep
quest.witch_coven.desc: Forest Witches have been hexing travelers who stray off the main path. The hex leaves people disoriented and lost for days. Confront three of them.
quest.witch_coven.accept.1: Three travelers this week came in from the east gate confused and sick. By the time they could speak again they all described the same thing — an old woman in the trees, watching them.
quest.witch_coven.accept.3: So the healers are saying. They go deep into the woods and they do not come out. The hexes they leave behind linger for days on the paths. Three covens have been spotted at different points. End their work in the forest and the roads east of here will be safe again.
quest.witch_coven.return.1: The hexed travelers all recovered this morning within an hour of each other. The healers said it was like a knot coming undone all at once. I do not understand it, but I know it means you succeeded. Here — the council agreed this warranted extra.
quest.whispering_woods_patrol.name: The Daily Patrol
quest.whispering_woods_patrol.desc: The Whispering Woods never stay clear for long. The rangers ask that any adventurer willing lend a hand keeping the main trails passable — kill five Forest Spiders and five Feral Dire Wolves.
quest.whispering_woods_patrol.accept.1: The rangers cannot cover every trail themselves. If you have the time, they have a standing request — keep the spiders and the dire wolves from reclaiming the paths. Five of each is the daily quota.
quest.whispering_woods_patrol.accept.3: Same reward as always, same task as always. The woods do not change. Come back when it is done.
quest.whispering_woods_patrol.return.1: The patrol confirmed it — paths are clear for another day. Same reward as always, and the rangers' thanks. Come back tomorrow if you are willing.
quest.job_smith_basics.name: The Smith's First Test
quest.job_smith_basics.desc: Gorhen wants to see that you understand the basics of the forge. Smelt three iron ingots and bring them to him.
quest.job_smith_basics.accept.1: You have chosen the smith's trade — good. Before I teach you anything more, I want to see three clean ingots from you. No slag, no cracks.
quest.job_smith_basics.accept.2: Iron ore into ingots. I know the process.
quest.job_smith_basics.accept.3: Knowing and doing are different things at a forge. Smelt three ingots and bring them to me. We start with the basics.
quest.job_smith_basics.return.1: Three ingots. Even pours, minimal waste. You understand heat better than most apprentices on their first week. Here is your due — and your next task.
quest.job_smith_forged.name: Iron in the Fire
quest.job_smith_forged.desc: Gorhen wants to see two iron swords — properly forged, not bought. Prove you can shape metal as well as melt it.
quest.job_smith_forged.accept.1: Smelting is just the beginning. What the forge is really for is shaping. I want two iron swords from you — not bought off my shelf, crafted from the ingots you smelt.
quest.job_smith_forged.accept.3: The recipe is straightforward — three ingots per blade. Watch your hammer angle on the fuller groove; that is where apprentices lose the edge alignment. Come back when both are done.
quest.job_smith_forged.return.1: Let me see those. Balance is right, edge is clean — the second one is better than the first, which tells me you were learning as you worked. That is exactly what I want to see. You are ready for heavier work.
quest.job_smith_armored.name: The Weight of Iron
quest.job_smith_armored.desc: Chain armor is the true test of a blacksmith's patience. Gorhen wants one finished suit.
quest.job_smith_armored.accept.1: Weapons come quickly once you have the rhythm. Armor is different. Chain armor means five ingots and a hundred small decisions about ring size, link tension, and overlap pattern.
quest.job_smith_armored.accept.2: That sounds like it takes time.
quest.job_smith_armored.accept.3: It does. That is the lesson. One finished suit, no shortcuts. When the town guard starts asking where their chainmail comes from, they will know your name.
quest.job_smith_armored.return.1: Solid links, even coverage, no gaps in the chest plate. I showed this to the guard captain this morning — he is already asking if you have more. Your name is getting around, smith. That is worth something.
quest.job_smith_mastery.name: The Smith's Mark
quest.job_smith_mastery.desc: Gorhen's final test: forge a steel sword. It requires the hardest alloy and the sharpest technique you have.
quest.job_smith_mastery.accept.1: I have one final test for you. Steel is not just harder iron — it is a different process entirely. The alloy demands beast material to stabilize the grain during the quench.
quest.job_smith_mastery.accept.2: Beast fangs. I have read about the technique.
quest.job_smith_mastery.accept.3: Then read your hands next — they will know if you did it right. Five ingots and two beast fangs. A steel sword. When you set your mark on a blade like that, the whole city will know a real smith lives here.
quest.job_smith_mastery.return.1: That edge will hold twice as long as iron. The balance point is exactly right. You are not my apprentice any more. You are a blacksmith, and this town is lucky to have you.
quest.job_leather_basics.name: Curing the Hide
quest.job_leather_basics.desc: The leathersmith wants to see that you can produce clean cured leather. Bring five pieces.
quest.job_leather_basics.accept.1: So you want to work leather. Good trade — the demand never drops. But before you touch a needle or a last, I want to see that you understand the basics of curing. Bring me five clean pieces of cured leather.
quest.job_leather_basics.accept.2: Two pieces of feral leather per cure. I know the ratio.
quest.job_leather_basics.accept.3: The ratio is easy. The patience is harder. Rushed curing cracks. Take your time with each piece and bring me five that are worth cutting.
quest.job_leather_basics.return.1: Even thickness, no splits at the edges. You waited long enough on the tanning — I can tell by the color. Five good hides. That is a solid start.
quest.job_leather_workshop.name: First Armor
quest.job_leather_workshop.desc: The leathersmith wants two finished leather vests — clean stitching, proper fit.
quest.job_leather_workshop.accept.1: Curing is just the raw material. Now we make something. I want two leather vests — four cured hides each. Stitching must be tight or the seams split the first time someone rolls to avoid a blade.
quest.job_leather_workshop.accept.3: You already know the difference — that tells me more than you think. Reinforced at the shoulder joins, standard on the sides. Bring me two and we will talk about the next step.
quest.job_leather_workshop.return.1: These will actually stop something. That shoulder join on the second one is tighter than the first — you adjusted between them. Good instinct. Rogues and hunters will pay well for work like this.
quest.job_leather_hunter.name: The Hunter's Commission
quest.job_leather_hunter.desc: The leathersmith has a commission from a hunter in town. Craft one hunter coat to fulfill it.
quest.job_leather_hunter.accept.1: A hunter came in asking for a proper coat. Evasion-lined, reinforced on the draw arm, good aim balance. The kind of work that takes four cured hides and two fangs for the quill-stitch trim.
quest.job_leather_hunter.accept.2: Fang trim on a coat. That is old-craft technique.
quest.job_leather_hunter.accept.3: Which is why she is paying well — and why I am giving the job to you. Fill the commission. If the hunter is happy, your reputation fills itself.
quest.job_leather_hunter.return.1: She tried it on this morning and barely said a word — just nodded and paid in full. That is the best review a hunter gives. Word will spread. Your name is worth something to these people now.
quest.job_miner_first_haul.name: Into the Vein
quest.job_miner_first_haul.desc: The mining master wants to see your first proper haul. Gather ten iron ore from the cave deposits.
quest.job_miner_first_haul.accept.1: The first thing a miner learns is that the cave does not owe you anything. You read the rock, you find the vein, you work it carefully, or you go home empty-handed.
quest.job_miner_first_haul.accept.2: I have a pickaxe and I know how to use it.
quest.job_miner_first_haul.accept.3: Then prove it. Ten pieces of iron ore from the cave deposits to the south. Look for the shimmering walls — that is where the iron runs. Come back when you have a full haul.
quest.job_miner_first_haul.return.1: Ten good chunks. You went for the rich seam, not the surface flaking — I can tell by the density. That is exactly right. You have a miner's eye. Here is what you are owed.
quest.job_miner_deep_vein.name: The Deep Seam
quest.job_miner_deep_vein.desc: The mining master wants a larger haul from deeper in the cave system. Gather twenty-five iron ore.
quest.job_miner_deep_vein.accept.1: The surface seams are thinning. The real ore is deeper — past the Chamber of Echoes, where the walls are wetter and the rock is darker. More dangerous, but the haul is worth it.
quest.job_miner_deep_vein.accept.2: I can handle the deeper tunnels.
quest.job_miner_deep_vein.accept.3: Twenty-five pieces. That is a commercial haul, not a training exercise. The forge masters in town will start noticing your name when ore like this comes in consistently.
quest.job_miner_deep_vein.return.1: Twenty-five ore and not a scratch on you. The smiths in the north quarter are already asking where the good deep-vein iron has been coming from. I told them it has a name. Here is your cut.
quest.job_miner_motherlode.name: The Motherlode
quest.job_miner_motherlode.desc: A master haul: fifty iron ore from the deepest accessible veins. The mining master wants to see if you have the endurance for it.
quest.job_miner_motherlode.accept.1: Most miners stop at twenty, twenty-five. They do the minimum and go home. The ones who become known — the ones the smiths come to by name — they do fifty in a single run.
quest.job_miner_motherlode.accept.2: Fifty ore. That is several trips, or one very long one.
quest.job_miner_motherlode.accept.3: One long one is better — your reading of the vein improves with every hour you spend down there. When you come back with fifty clean chunks, every craftsman in Hydea will know who to call when the forge runs low.
quest.job_miner_motherlode.return.1: Fifty. And the quality is consistent all the way through — you did not rush toward the end. The forge master sent a message this morning asking if you were available for a standing supply order. That is what a reputation looks like.
quest.job_woodcutter_first_timber.name: First Fell
quest.job_woodcutter_first_timber.desc: The woodcutter master at the forest sawmill wants your first proper timber run. Gather ten pieces of wood.
quest.job_woodcutter_first_timber.accept: You want to learn woodcutting? Good trade. The forest here is generous if you work it right. First lesson: never take from a living grove. Fell from the edge, take the deadwood first, let the interior grow.
Managed felling. I understand the principle.
Principle is a start. Ten pieces of timber from the forest to the east. The pine edge is easiest for a first run. Come back when you have a full bundle.
quest.job_woodcutter_first_timber.return: Clean cuts, no bark left on the face grain. You felled smart — I can tell by which trees are still standing. Ten good pieces. The sawmill can use every one of these.
quest.job_woodcutter_lumber_run.name: The Lumber Run
quest.job_woodcutter_lumber_run.desc: A proper supply run: twenty-five pieces of timber for the sawmill. The woodcutter master wants to see you work at scale.
quest.job_woodcutter_lumber_run.accept.1: Ten pieces is a test. Twenty-five is a job. The town carpenter has a commission for new floor joists — he needs timber and he needs it reliable.
quest.job_woodcutter_lumber_run.accept.2: Twenty-five pieces. I can handle that.
quest.job_woodcutter_lumber_run.accept.3: The oak sections of the hollow are better for load-bearing work. Pine for cladding. Choose the right wood for the right purpose and the carpenter will come back to you personally next time.
quest.job_woodcutter_lumber_run.return.1: The carpenter sorted through this in under an hour. He said you selected the right wood for load-bearing without being told — he noticed. Building a reputation is mostly about people noticing the right things. You are doing that.
quest.job_woodcutter_forest_supply.name: Forest Supply Contract
quest.job_woodcutter_forest_supply.desc: The sawmill has a standing order from the town builders. Fill it with fifty pieces of timber.
quest.job_woodcutter_forest_supply.accep: The town builders put a standing supply contract through the sawmill this week. Fifty pieces of mixed timber — pine, oak, whatever the hollow and the edge can spare responsibly. This is real work now, not training.
I know you will. When you come back with fifty, I am going to put your name on the contract instead of mine. The builders will know who to call when they break ground on anything new in this town.
quest.job_woodcutter_forest_supply.retur: Fifty pieces, sorted and bundled. The builders sent word this afternoon — they accepted the whole load without inspection. When they trust the work that much, they stop asking questions. Your name is on the contract. Welcome to the trade.
quest.unsave_caves.name: Disappearance of Townsfolk
quest.unsave_caves.desc: The Trolls and Goblins in the Deep Caves are getting restless, kill some to keep them at bay.
quest.unsave_caves.accept.1: Adventurer, please — people from town have been going missing at night. The caves to the south are the cause, I am certain of it.
quest.unsave_caves.accept.3: Six families in the last fortnight alone. The Goblins and Trolls down there have grown bold. If you could cut their numbers — ten Goblins and ten Trolls — we might finally sleep safely again.
quest.unsave_caves.return.1: You have returned! The night watch reported no screaming last night for the first time in weeks. Here, take this — you have more than earned it.
quest.cave_bats.name: Squeaky Problem
quest.cave_bats.desc: The bats in the deeper tunnels have grown aggressive — travellers report being dive-bombed the moment they leave the main passage. Clear some of them out.
quest.cave_bats.accept.1: The miners refuse to go deeper than the entrance passage. Every time they try, the bats dive at them in swarms.
quest.cave_bats.accept.3: Eight should be enough to scatter the rest. The miners need those ore veins desperately. Come back when it is done.
quest.cave_bats.return.1: The miners are already back at work — I can hear them from here. Whatever you did to those bats, it worked. This reward was waiting for you.
quest.stone_imps.name: Rocky Nuisance
quest.stone_imps.desc: Stone Imps have been pilfering tools and supplies left near the cave entrance. Find them in the deeper tunnels and put a stop to it.
quest.stone_imps.accept.1: Now it is the Stone Imps. They have been sneaking out of the deeper tunnels and making off with tools and supplies near the cave entrance. Our whole stockpile is nearly gone.
quest.stone_imps.accept.3: Ten of the little thieves ought to do it. Without their numbers they will not dare to venture near the entrance again. Thank you, truly.
quest.stone_imps.return.1: The supply crates are finally safe again! The miners already restocked the entrance cache. You have my thanks — and this reward.
quest.wraith_problem.name: Wraith Problem
quest.wraith_problem.desc: Kill the Wraith in the Chamber of the Hollow Crypt!
quest.wraith_problem.accept.1: That Wraith haunting the Chamber of the Hollow Crypt is driving travelers away from the whole passage south of town.
quest.wraith_problem.accept.3: Ten encounters should be enough to push it back for a while. And please, come again when it returns — the menace never stays gone for long, and the reward still stands.
quest.wraith_problem.return.1: The road south is passable again. Merchants have already started using it. You have done this town a real service — same reward whenever it grows bold again.
quest.bone_crawlers.name: What Lies Beneath
quest.bone_crawlers.desc: Something is raising the dead in the ancient chamber below the abyss passage. The Bone Crawlers are spreading upward — deal with them before they reach the main tunnels.
quest.bone_crawlers.accept.1: Something terrible is stirring below the Abyss passage. The miners who came back spoke of bones moving on their own — Bone Crawlers, clawing their way upward.
quest.bone_crawlers.accept.2: If they reach the main tunnels the whole cave network is lost. You must destroy fifteen of them before they spread.
quest.bone_crawlers.accept.3: I understand. I will push them back.
quest.bone_crawlers.return.1: The bones are still again — for now. Whatever was raising them seems to have retreated. Remarkable work — here is your reward.
quest.lizzard_raids_1.name: Unsafe Roads
quest.lizzard_raids_1.desc: The Maka Maka make the northwest road between Hydea and Royas unsafe for travelers, we have to push them back!
quest.lizzard_raids_1.accept.1: Traveler, the north road to Royas has become treacherous. The Maka Maka have been raiding caravans — three lost this season alone.
quest.lizzard_raids_1.accept.3: They control the valley passes north of the city. Clear fifteen warriors and ten scouts and the road should open again. When you are done, find Aldric in Royas — he will have your reward ready.
quest.lizzard_raids_1.return.1: The road through the valley is open again! The first caravan in weeks arrived safely this morning. Mira told us you would be coming. Here, this was set aside for you the moment we heard.
quest.boar_hunting.name: Dangerous Boars
quest.boar_hunting.desc: The Townsfolk is worried about the Mossy Boars, please kill a few so they can feel safe again.
quest.boar_hunting.accept.1: The Mossy Boars in the highland passes have been charging at anyone who comes through. Three travelers were gored just last week.
quest.boar_hunting.accept.2: How many need to be culled?
quest.boar_hunting.accept.3: Twenty-five should bring the herd under control. When you have finished, head to Royas and speak with Aldric — he will see you are properly rewarded.
quest.boar_hunting.return.1: The highland passes are safe again. The shepherds were the first to notice — their flocks came back unscathed this morning. Mira sends her regards, and this reward is long overdue.
quest.end_the_undying.name: End the Undying
quest.end_the_undying.desc: Defeat the Lich lurking at the end of the Hollow Crypt.
quest.end_the_undying.accept.1: I thought the Wraith was the worst of it, but the miners found something deeper in the crypt. A Lich — something ancient and undying.
quest.end_the_undying.accept.2: A Lich? That is no small task.
quest.end_the_undying.accept.3: I know. But you are the only adventurer capable enough. If you can destroy it, this town — and every traveler who passes through — will owe you everything. The reward reflects that.
quest.end_the_undying.return.1: Is it truly gone? The Lich is destroyed? Word has already spread through the whole town. What you have done today will be remembered long after either of us is gone. Please, take this — it is the least Hydea can offer.
quest.ceralith_spirit_hunters.name: Spirit Hunters
quest.ceralith_spirit_hunters.desc: River Spirits have been ambushing ferrymen and travelers along the Cera waterways. Slay five and restore safe passage.
quest.ceralith_spirit_hunters.accept.1: The ferrymen refuse to cross the river since the River Spirits started appearing at the shallows. Three boats capsized last week alone.
quest.ceralith_spirit_hunters.accept.2: How many are we talking about?
quest.ceralith_spirit_hunters.accept.3: Five should scatter the rest. They respond to aggression — once their numbers drop they pull back to deeper water. The reward is modest, but the ferryman's guild will owe you a favor.
quest.ceralith_spirit_hunters.return.1: The ferries are running again — I heard the first crossing went smooth as glass this morning. The guild sends their thanks, and here is what I promised.
quest.valley_wolves.name: Shadow in the Valley
quest.valley_wolves.desc: Shadow Wolves have been hunting travelers and livestock along the valley roads south of Royas. Drive them back.
quest.valley_wolves.accept.1: Since the Maka Maka pulled back, the Shadow Wolves have been moving in. Farmers are losing sheep and the south road is getting dangerous at dusk.
quest.valley_wolves.accept.3: That should break up the main pack. They hunt together — take enough out and the rest will scatter into the hills. Careful at night; they are faster than they look.
quest.valley_wolves.return.1: The shepherds came in this morning saying the fields were quiet all night. You have done them a real kindness. Here is your reward.
quest.treant_blight.name: The Blight Spreads
quest.treant_blight.desc: A sickness is twisting the old trees at the Whispering Woods edge into Withered Treants. Cut them down before the blight reaches the farmland.
quest.treant_blight.accept.1: The treeline on the south road has gone dark. Farmers are calling them Withered Treants — old forest spirits twisted by blight. Six of the things have already uprooted themselves and started moving toward the fields.
quest.treant_blight.accept.3: Careful — their bark is thick and their roots hit hard. Take your time, do not rush them. Six should be enough to stop the spread from reaching the farmland.
quest.treant_blight.return.1: The treeline has stilled. No more movement, no more cracking wood in the night. The farmers are breathing easier. Thank you — here is your reward.
quest.bandit_pass.name: Cleanse the Pass
quest.bandit_pass.desc: Bandit Marauders have seized the highland pass south of Royas and are taxing every caravan at sword-point. Clear them out.
quest.bandit_pass.accept.1: The highland pass is gone. Bandit Marauders — at least a dozen of them — set up a blockade three days ago. No caravan has moved since.
quest.bandit_pass.accept.3: Ten of them and the rest will break and run. They are hired blades, not true soldiers — they have no loyalty when the numbers shift against them. Watch for the archers on the high ground.
quest.bandit_pass.return.1: The first caravan arrived this morning — intact, not a coin missing. The merchants are already calling you the Hero of the Pass. Here, this comes from the merchant council's fund.
quest.ceralith_cellar.name: Infestation Below
quest.ceralith_cellar.desc: Plague Rats have overrun the grain cellars beneath Royas. The town's food stores are at risk — root them out.
quest.ceralith_cellar.accept.1: We have a crisis. The grain cellars are overrun with Plague Rats — not regular rats, these things are huge and diseased. Two storekeepers are already sick.
quest.ceralith_cellar.accept.3: Fifteen at minimum before the colony gets too large to stop naturally. Cover your face — their bites fester fast. The food stores for this whole season are at risk.
quest.ceralith_cellar.return.1: The cellars are clear! The town healer said no new cases of the sickness since you went down. We can finally start salvaging what stores were not spoiled. Here — the whole council chipped in for this.
quest.woods_rangers.name: Phantom Arrows
quest.woods_rangers.desc: Dread Archers have been picking off the Hydea forest rangers from the tree canopy. Track them through the Whispering Woods and put them down.
quest.woods_rangers.accept.1: We have lost four rangers in the Whispering Woods this week. Shadow arrows, no tracks, nothing. The other rangers are calling them Dread Archers — spirits that haunt the old paths.
quest.woods_rangers.accept.2: I know that kind of creature. They vanish after they shoot.
quest.woods_rangers.accept.3: Then you know how to deal with them. Ten, and the woods should be passable again. Close range is your best bet — they cannot vanish once you are in on them. The rangers are counting on you.
quest.woods_rangers.return.1: The patrol returned this morning — all of them, not a scratch. They said the forest felt different, quieter in the right way. What you did in there will not be forgotten. Here is the reward from the ranger's guild.
quest.hollow_awakening.name: The Hollow Stirs
quest.hollow_awakening.desc: Hollow Knights have awakened in the deep forest hollow and are marching outward. Stop them before they reach the roads.
quest.hollow_awakening.accept.1: Something ancient has woken in the forest hollow. The rangers are calling them Hollow Knights — armored husks, no soul inside, just the curse driving them forward.
quest.hollow_awakening.accept.3: Five is all we can confirm. There may be more, but five down and the advance will stall — they seem to move together. Hit them hard; they do not feel pain and they do not stop. The reward comes from the city council directly.
quest.hollow_awakening.return.1: The hollow is still again. The patrol found five empty suits in the mud — whatever was driving them has retreated. The council is grateful. This is just the start of what you are owed.
quest.void_tide.name: The Void Tide
quest.void_tide.desc: Void Wraiths are seeping through a rift near the mountain plateau, growing in number each night. Seal the tide by destroying eight of them.
quest.void_tide.accept.1: They are calling it the Void Tide. Wraiths not of this world — they seep through the air like smoke and drain the warmth from anything they touch. The rift near the plateau is spreading.
quest.void_tide.accept.2: Destroy enough of them and the rift starves.
quest.void_tide.accept.3: That is the theory. Eight should weaken it enough that it closes on its own. Do not let them surround you — they feed on each other's presence and hit harder in groups.
quest.void_tide.return.1: The rift has narrowed — the scouts can barely see it now. Whatever you did up there, it worked. Xarra thanks you. Here is the full reward.
quest.harpy_crossings.name: Harpy Crossings
quest.harpy_crossings.desc: Storm Harpies have been grounding all air couriers and attacking the mountain pass road. Silence them.
quest.harpy_crossings.accept.1: The mountain pass has been closed for two weeks. Storm Harpies — six of them at least — have taken the high cliffs and they dive at anything that moves through the pass.
quest.harpy_crossings.accept.2: Six of them. That will take some work.
quest.harpy_crossings.accept.3: They ride lightning, so do not try to outlast them in the open. Strike fast and move between cover. The courier guild is offering a generous sum — their whole operation depends on that pass.
quest.harpy_crossings.return.1: The couriers flew through this morning — first time in weeks! The guild master nearly wept. Here is everything promised, and then some. You have opened Xarra's throat again.
quest.ancient_guardians.name: Ancient Guardians
quest.ancient_guardians.desc: Three Elder Golems have awakened beneath the plateau and are cracking the foundations of the road above. Bring them down.
quest.ancient_guardians.accept.1: The road engineers came to me this morning white-faced. Three Elder Golems have risen from beneath the plateau — ancient constructs, the size of houses, and they are walking into the foundations of the main road.
quest.ancient_guardians.accept.3: No one knows. They have been down there for centuries. Three of them — and you will need every skill you have. They are slow, but each strike is final. The city's road infrastructure depends on you stopping them.
quest.ancient_guardians.return.1: The tremors stopped an hour ago. The engineers went down and found three collapsed piles of stone. Remarkable. The road is intact. Xarra owes you more than gold — but this is the best we can do for now.
quest.crimson_hunt.name: The Crimson Hunt
quest.crimson_hunt.desc: A Crimson Drake has descended from the high peaks and claimed the plateau. It must be driven off before it reaches the city.
quest.crimson_hunt.accept.1: We have a problem unlike anything this city has faced in a generation. A Crimson Drake — young, but large enough to be deadly — has landed on the plateau and killed three scouting parties.
quest.crimson_hunt.accept.2: A drake. Not quite a dragon, but close enough.
quest.crimson_hunt.accept.3: Close enough that we cannot field soldiers against it. You have handled everything the road has thrown at you so far. This is the final test. Bring it down and the plateau is ours again.
quest.crimson_hunt.return.1: You killed a Crimson Drake. I did not think I would say those words in my lifetime. The plateau is clear, the scouts have confirmed it. Xarra will remember this day. Take this — it is everything the council could authorize, and it is not enough.
