job.woodcutter.name: Woodcutter
job.woodcutter.desc: Harvest timber from forests and sell lumber to carpenters and builders across the realm.
job.miner.name: Miner
job.miner.desc: Delve into caves and quarries to extract ore, gems, and stone for crafting and trade.
job.herbalist.name: Herbalist
job.herbalist.desc: Collect rare plants and herbs used in alchemy, medicine, and magical rituals.
job.blacksmith.name: Blacksmith
job.blacksmith.desc: Forge weapons, armour, and tools from raw metals. Mastery unlocks rarer alloys and enchantable gear.
job.alchemist.name: Alchemist
job.alchemist.desc: Brew potions, elixirs, and transmutation reagents from gathered herbs and minerals.
job.cook.name: Cook
job.cook.desc: Prepare meals that grant temporary buffs to adventurers. Higher skill unlocks more powerful recipes.
job.leathersmith.name: Leathersmith
job.leathersmith.desc: Work hides and pelts into supple armour, cloaks, and footwear for rogues and hunters.
job.tailor.name: Tailor
job.tailor.desc: Weave cloth and sew robes worn by clerics, mages, and druids. Higher skill yields finer magical fabrics.
job.artificer.name: Artificer
job.artificer.desc: Craft rings, bands, and trinkets that channel latent power. Mastery unlocks rarer gemstone settings.
job.enchanter.name: Enchanter
job.enchanter.desc: Imbue staves, tomes, and magical weapons with arcane energy. A rare and sought-after craft.
race.Rotuka.desc: Powerful and enduring warriors of the harsh northern wastes. High strength and endurance, but low affinity for magic.
race.Iymva.desc: Swift and dexterous hunters of the deep forests. Unmatched agility, though fragile under prolonged assault.
race.Myralu.desc: Adaptable scholars and combatants who balance body and mind. A well-rounded people suited to any path.
race.Zalu.desc: Stoic wanderers from the great plains. No innate advantages or weaknesses — their strength lies in steady, reliable growth.
race.Gavon.desc: Mystics with an ancient bond to spirit and intellect. Frail of body but commanding in magic and spirit.
race.Gamato.desc: Versatile craftspeople and traders. Modest bonuses across all stats make them dependable in any role.
race.Amato.desc: Humans — curious, adaptable, and uniquely attuned to runic magic. Their access to the Runic Mage class is unmatched by other races.
item.soulbound_phylactery.desc: A vessel once used to anchor the Lich's soul. It radiates unstable magical power, drawn from death itself.
item.steel_sword.desc: A balanced sword for melee fighters.
item.leather_bow.desc: A light bow ideal for agile archers.
item.flamecaster_staff.desc: A staff imbued with flame runes, enhancing magic power.
item.storm_robes.desc: Flowing robes crackling with arcane wind energy.
item.crystal_focus_band.desc: A magical circlet that sharpens focus and channels power.
item.beast_fang.desc: A large, sharp fang from a feral creature.
item.beast_flesh.desc: Tough raw meat from a wild monster.
item.feral_leather.desc: Rough leather from a savage beast.
item.earth_essence.desc: The concentrated core of an Earth Elemental.
item.stone_fragment.desc: A jagged piece of living stone.
item.stone.desc: A plain chunk of quarried stone, useful for crafting.
item.fire_ash.desc: What remains of a defeated Fire Elemental.
item.wind_whisper.desc: An ethereal fragment carried by a Wind Elemental.
item.water_bead.desc: A liquid orb pulsing with magical water energy.
item.spirit_dust.desc: Fine dust left behind by a banished spirit.
item.shadow_remnant.desc: A dark, swirling wisp of condensed shadow energy.
item.iron_ingot.desc: A bar of smelted iron, ready for forging into weapons or armour.
item.iron_sword.desc: A sturdy sword forged from iron ingots.
item.chain_armor.desc: Interlocked iron rings woven into a flexible suit of armour.
item.pickaxe.desc: Used to mine ores at gathering spots.
item.woodcutter_axe.desc: Used to chop trees at gathering spots.
item.iron_ore.desc: A chunk of iron-rich rock, useful for crafting.
item.wood.desc: A rough-cut piece of timber, useful for crafting and construction.
item.sunleaf.desc: A rare herb found near sunlight cracks.
item.cured_leather.desc: Tanned and treated hide, ready to be worked into armour or accessories.
item.leather_vest.desc: Supple leather armour offering good protection without sacrificing mobility.
item.bolt_of_cloth.desc: Woven fabric sold by the tailor. Used to sew robes and cloaks.
item.linen_robe.desc: A simply cut robe that offers modest magical protection.
item.imbued_ring.desc: A plain iron ring set with an earth-stone shard, granting a steady surge of vitality.
item.mages_tome.desc: A grimoire dense with arcane script. Focusing through it sharpens magical precision.
item.tempered_blade.desc: A carefully tempered weapon made for adventurers who have outgrown starter steel.
item.vanguard_mail.desc: Reinforced mail with a padded underlayer, built to hold against mid-tier monsters.
item.swiftsteel_edge.desc: A light, quick weapon balanced for precision strikes and mobile fighting.
item.stalkers_leather.desc: Layered leather gear that protects without dulling movement.
item.runed_staff.desc: A staff etched with simple channeling runes for steadier spell power.
item.sage_robes.desc: Warded robes that reinforce both mana flow and magical protection.
item.champions_seal.desc: A sturdy seal worn by practiced fighters as proof of hard-won victories.
item.focus_crystal.desc: A polished crystal charm that steadies magic under pressure.
monster.marsh_viper.name: Marsh Viper
monster.marsh_viper.desc: A slender river snake that strikes from the shallows with surprising speed. Its fangs carry a mild venom.
monster.river_toad.name: River Toad
monster.river_toad.desc: A hulking amphibian that lurks in the muddy banks. It is slow to move but delivers a crushing blow with its powerful legs.
monster.maka_maka_youth.name: Maka Maka Youth
monster.maka_maka_youth.desc: A young member of the Maka Maka tribe still learning the ways of the hunt. Eager to prove themselves, but not yet a seasoned warrior.
quest.royas_vipers.name: Marsh Viper Infestation
quest.royas_vipers.desc: Marsh Vipers are nesting too close to the village paths. Clear out five before someone gets bitten.
quest.royas_vipers.accept.1: The vipers are getting bolder. Two farmhands have been bitten this week alone — our healer is running low on antidote.
quest.royas_vipers.accept.2: How many do you need cleared?
quest.royas_vipers.accept.3: Five ought to scatter the rest of the nest. Stay away from the marsh reeds — that is where they cluster.
quest.royas_vipers.return.1: No new bites since you cleared them out. That ought to hold the rest back for a while. Here — as promised.
quest.royas_toads.name: Toad Tide
quest.royas_toads.desc: River Toads have been fouling the wells and spoiling fish traps along the Cera. Drive them back.
quest.royas_toads.accept.1: The river toads are massing near the wells and the fish traps are ruined. I am not even sure what draws them this close.
quest.royas_toads.accept.3: Six should scatter the colony. Mind the slick mud by the bank — they spit.
quest.royas_toads.return.1: The wells are clear and the traps are holding again. Good work — here is what I owe you.
quest.royas_youth_threat.name: Young Scouts
quest.royas_youth_threat.desc: Maka Maka Youth have been spotted scouting the outskirts. Thin their numbers before their elders take notice.
quest.royas_youth_threat.accept.1: Those are Maka Maka youth out by the eastern path — not raiding yet, just watching. That is how it starts.
quest.royas_youth_threat.accept.2: You want me to drive them off?
quest.royas_youth_threat.accept.3: Five of them. Hit hard enough that they carry word back. The older ones listen when the young do not come home.
quest.royas_youth_threat.return.1: Word must have spread — no new sightings since yesterday. Well done.
quest.royas_thornhoppers.name: Thorn Menace
quest.royas_thornhoppers.desc: Thornhoppers are destroying the eastern crop fields. The harvest cannot survive another season of this.
quest.royas_thornhoppers.accept.1: The crop fields on the eastern slope are being torn apart by Thornhoppers. Old Marek lost half his yield already.
quest.royas_thornhoppers.accept.3: Six, yes. Be careful — the thorns they kick up can get into your eyes. Watch where you step.
quest.royas_thornhoppers.return.1: Marek saw you coming back and nearly wept. The fields are safe for now. Take this — the council contributed.
quest.royas_river_raptors.name: River Predators
quest.royas_river_raptors.desc: River Raptors have been ambushing travelers crossing the highland roads. Clear the threat.
quest.royas_river_raptors.accept.1: Three traders missed their arrival this week. The ones who did make it said River Raptors hit them on the highland road.
quest.royas_river_raptors.accept.2: Ambush predators. Five on the road — I can track them.
quest.royas_river_raptors.accept.3: That is what I was hoping to hear. The road trade keeps this village alive.
quest.royas_river_raptors.return.1: A courier came through this morning — said the road felt clear for the first time in weeks. You have my thanks.
quest.royas_maka_scouts.name: Scouting Party
quest.royas_maka_scouts.desc: Maka Maka Scouts are mapping the village defenses. Drive them off before their war party arrives.
quest.royas_maka_scouts.accept.1: Seven Maka Maka Scouts, moving in formation. They are not hunting — they are counting walls and counting heads.
quest.royas_maka_scouts.accept.2: I will send them running before they finish their count.
quest.royas_maka_scouts.accept.3: Go fast. If they complete their survey, the hunters come next.
quest.royas_maka_scouts.return.1: No scouts since you left. Whatever they planned, they are planning it somewhere else now.
quest.royas_river_spirits.name: Spirits of the Cera
quest.royas_river_spirits.desc: River Spirits have cursed the ford crossing and the ferry has not run in days. Drive them from the Cera.
quest.royas_river_spirits.accept.1: The ferry has not run in four days. The River Spirits cursed the crossing — Aldric says he heard them singing in the shallows at night.
quest.royas_river_spirits.accept.2: Four ought to break the pattern.
quest.royas_river_spirits.accept.3: The ferrymen will not cross until they are gone. This village needs that ferry.
quest.royas_river_spirits.return.1: The ferry is running again — Aldric made his first crossing at dawn and came back safe. I cannot thank you enough.
quest.royas_maka_hunters.name: Hunters at the Gate
quest.royas_maka_hunters.desc: The Maka Maka Hunters have arrived and struck the northern farms at dawn. Push them back.
quest.royas_maka_hunters.accept.1: They came at sunrise. Six Maka Maka Hunters hit the north farm and took livestock. The family barely got out.
quest.royas_maka_hunters.accept.2: They will not get a second hit.
quest.royas_maka_hunters.accept.3: If you can drive them back before dark, we still have a chance to salvage what they left behind.
quest.royas_maka_hunters.return.1: The north farm is quiet now. The family came back this morning to count what they had left. You saved this village a hard winter.
quest.royas_highland_patrol.name: Highland Patrol
quest.royas_highland_patrol.desc: The highland roads need regular clearing. A standing bounty for anyone willing to keep the passes safe.
quest.royas_highland_patrol.accept.1: The patrol route needs clearing again. Thornhoppers on the lower path and Maka Maka youth at the ridge — the usual trouble.
quest.royas_highland_patrol.accept.3: Three of each should be enough for now. Come back when it is done.
quest.royas_highland_patrol.return.1: Clean work, as always. The patrol route is yours whenever you want the coin.
monster.mudcrawler.name: Mudcrawler
monster.mudcrawler.desc: A fat, armored grub that wallows through the wet lowland soil. Slow and dim, but its shell can take a few hits before it yields.
monster.swamp_leech.name: Swamp Leech
monster.swamp_leech.desc: A slick, finger-long parasite that clings to the underside of reeds and waiting stones. Quick to latch on, quick to drain.
monster.bramble_hound.name: Bramble Hound
monster.bramble_hound.desc: A lean, feral dog that has gone half-wild in the undergrowth. Runs in loose packs and bites harder than its size suggests.
quest.royas_mudcrawlers.name: Mud in the Channels
quest.royas_mudcrawlers.desc: Mudcrawlers have been burrowing through the irrigation channels and clogging them with packed earth. Clear five of them out.
quest.royas_mudcrawlers.accept.1: Something has been getting into the lower irrigation channels — clogging them with loose dirt and shell fragments.
quest.royas_mudcrawlers.accept.3: Mudcrawlers. Fat armored grubs that burrow through wet soil. Five should be enough to clear the worst of it — they nest near the water's edge.
quest.royas_mudcrawlers.return.1: The channel is already running clearer — the farmers noticed this morning. Good work, here is what we agreed.
quest.co1_mudcrawler_remedy.name: Healer's Request
quest.co1_mudcrawler_remedy.desc: The healer needs mudcrawler carapace to grind into an antiseptic compound. Bring down four of them near the marsh.
quest.co1_mudcrawler_remedy.accept.1: Those mudcrawlers in the lower marsh — their shell casing makes a fine antiseptic when ground and mixed right. I need four cleared so I can collect the pieces.
quest.co1_mudcrawler_remedy.accept.2: Four mudcrawlers. Near the south road?
quest.co1_mudcrawler_remedy.accept.3: Follow the path and look for soft soil near the water's edge. They burrow shallow — you will find them easily enough.
quest.co1_mudcrawler_remedy.return.1: The shell will dry out by tomorrow and I can start the grinding. This ought to keep the wound infection rate down through the season. Thank you — take this.
quest.co1_leech_problem.name: Fouled Water
quest.co1_leech_problem.desc: Swamp Leeches have overrun the marsh pools upstream. The healer needs them thinned before they contaminate the lower water supply.
quest.co1_leech_problem.accept.1: The water has been off for three days. Swamp leeches upstream, fouling the flow. Six should be enough to break the infestation.
quest.co1_leech_problem.accept.3: They cluster under the surface near reeds and submerged roots. Step carefully — they do not warn you before they strike.
quest.co1_leech_problem.return.1: The water tested clean this morning. You may have just saved the village from a bad month. Here — this comes from the town health fund.
quest.co1_hound_pack.name: Teeth on the Road
quest.co1_hound_pack.desc: A pack of Bramble Hounds has been harassing travelers on the road south of town. Drive them back before someone gets seriously hurt.
quest.co1_hound_pack.accept.1: A peddler came in this morning with bite marks on his arm and his pack half-empty. Bramble Hounds hit him on the south road — five of them running together now, bold as you like.
quest.co1_hound_pack.accept.2: Five of them on the road. I can clear that.
quest.co1_hound_pack.accept.3: Hit fast before they scatter — if they split up you will be chasing them all afternoon.
quest.co1_hound_pack.return.1: The peddler came back through this afternoon and said the road was clean. No signs of the pack. You have my thanks — here is what I promised.
room.royas.desc: A small mountain village at the meeting point of the Nuvmito trail and the Grelmito path.
room.novmito.1.desc: The trail flattens as it reaches the valley floor. The smoke from Royas is visible ahead — probably Taro's forge, running before dawn as always. From here the village looks like a handful of stone houses set against the mountain wall, almost indistinguishable from the rock it was built from.
room.novmito.2.desc: The gradient eases and the valley floor stretches ahead. The Xaryre peaks flank both sides of the path; ahead, the valley widens where Royas sits in its hollow. Pine gives way to mixed forest on the lower slopes. The sound of the Breswelc is just audible from somewhere to the west.
room.novmito.3.desc: The trail drops steeply through switchbacks cut into the slope. Loose stone and exposed roots make the footing treacherous after rain. Below, the valley floor is closer but still far enough to feel remote. The peaks of the Xaryre press close on both sides.
room.novmito.turn.desc: The Nuvmito crosses a minor ridge here and the trail turns south. The eastern valley is suddenly visible below — a long green slash between the ranges, with Royas somewhere at its center. The descent begins. The trail narrows as it finds the first switchbacks down the southern face.
room.novmito.4.desc: The Nuvmito trail leaves Hydea's eastern gate and immediately begins crossing the upper Xaryre foothills. The city fades quickly behind rock and pine. The trail is narrow but well-worn — generations of foot traffic between Hydea and the valley settlements has kept it passable. The path rises as it moves east.
room.novmito.5.desc: The Nuvmito trail levels out as Hydea comes into view across the foothills. The stones underfoot are worn by generations of traders, miners, and valley folk making the crossing between city and mountain settlements.
room.hydea.east.desc: The eastern district of Hydea is where the Nuvmito trail begins — the old crossing path that links the city to the valley settlements across the northern Xaryre. Travellers heading east carry mountain goods and return with valley produce. A woodcutter's post marks the city's eastern boundary; beyond it, the foothills open onto the trail head.
room.hydea.center.desc: Hydea stands at the foot of the northern Xaryre, the Breswelc river audible from every corner of the city. The main square is lined with thick-walled stone buildings, their construction as much fortress as town. Traders from the lowlands haggle with mountain miners, and off-duty soldiers watch from doorways. The weight of what is happening to the west has reached even here.
room.hydea.south.desc: The southern gate drops away from Hydea into the first hard descent of the mountain road. City noise fades quickly here, replaced by wind, stone, and the long view toward the pass system below.
room.hydea.north.desc: The northern gate of Hydea faces toward the Trevyre foothills. Beyond the walls, sawmills and logging camps stretch along the tree line. The smell of fresh-cut pine mixes with forge smoke. Miners return through here in the evenings, carrying iron from the foothills caves. The gate road leads north into the lower Trevyre range — a direction few travel without purpose.
room.hydea.mines.desc: The mine district sits at the northern edge of Hydea, just beyond the northern gate. The shaft entrance descends into the iron-bearing rock of the Xaryre foothills — the source of most of the city's iron trade. The company offices and ore-sorting sheds line the road. Past the district, the Trevyre foothills begin their climb.
room.cave.entrance.desc: A reinforced shaft entrance cut into the Xaryre foothills north of Hydea. The city's main iron supply comes through here. Cold air drifts from the dark ahead; the smell of stone and ore is thick at the threshold.
room.cave.dark_passage.desc: The passage narrows to shoulder-width and the light from the entrance vanishes. The next chamber is visible only as a faint brightening in the distance. The walls are close enough to touch on both sides; the ore veins here run unbroken.
room.cave.chamber_echoes.desc: A chamber where sound behaves strangely — footsteps multiply, whispers carry from across the room. Iron seams run through every wall. The city mining company has been working this chamber for forty years; whatever unease the acoustics cause, the yield overrides it.
room.cave.junction.desc: The tunnel splits here. One direction leads back toward the upper mine and daylight. The other descends toward a lower section the company's surveyors mapped and then quietly declined to develop. The cold from below is noticeably sharper.
room.cave.chamber_ancient.desc: Ancient glyphs worn smooth by centuries of moisture cover every surface. Whatever was once kept or worshipped here is long gone — only bones remain. The stone-cutting method visible in the walls is not the same as the mine above; someone else was working this rock, long before iron was the reason anyone came down here.
room.cave.chamber_deep.desc: The cave widens into a proper chamber, its ceiling swallowed by shadow. The mining company's survey marks stop at the entry to this room. Faintly glowing fungi cling to the walls and the air smells of damp stone and something older — older than the mine, older than Hydea itself.
room.cave.abyss_passage.desc: Glowing fungi have colonized this stretch of passage — their light is faint blue and cold. Beyond them, the tunnel drops into territory that the mining company officially does not send workers into. The air here tastes different: older.
room.cave.chamber_hollow.desc: The passage opens into a natural hollow that someone, long ago, shaped into something more deliberate. The walls have been worked — not by mining tools. A carved lintel still stands above a low doorway cut into the far wall. Whatever is beyond it is not part of the mine.
room.grelmito.1.desc: The Grelmito path runs along the valley's eastern face immediately south of Royas. Farmland terraces carved into the lower slopes give way to rougher country as the trail climbs south. A few isolated homesteads dot the hillside — farmers who chose distance from the village over ease of access.
room.grelmito.2.desc: A bare rise where the trees thin and the sky opens. From this height you can see across the valley to where Royas lies in its hollow below the peaks. Further south the valley narrows toward Gerlyas. An old stone post here — too eroded to read any inscription — marks where the valley trail begins its descent toward the deeper reaches of the Grelmito.
room.gerlyas.desc: Gerlyas is quieter than Royas — fewer people, fewer fires, fewer words spoken to strangers. The valley narrows here and the sun is gone by early afternoon. The inhabitants remember things the rest of the valley has quietly forgotten: the names of the peaks, the old protocols for approaching a dragon's mountain, the shape of a carved wing in the oldest stone in the village. No dragons have been seen here in longer than anyone can say. The stories remain.
room.whispering_woods.1.desc: The Whispering Woods begin at the junction where the Grelmito path meets the forest edge. The transition is immediate — the valley disappears behind the treeline within a few steps. The old-growth canopy closes overhead and the temperature drops. The constant soft sound that names the forest is present here from the first step inside.
room.whispering_woods.2.desc: The forest deepens. The characteristic sound that gives the woods their name is present here in full — wind through the high canopy, constant and low, just below articulate. The trees here are enormous, their trunks wider than two arm-spans. The path continues south through old-growth oak and pine.
room.whispering_woods.3.desc: The path twists between roots thick enough to trip a cart wheel. The trees stand close together, their bark dark with age and damp, and the forest sound gathers here into a low, steady murmur.
room.whispering_woods.4.desc: The southern end of the Whispering Woods. The canopy thins and the mountain terrain reasserts itself — exposed stone, shorter trees, open sky. A path leads east from here toward the junction south of Gerlyas, connecting to the route toward the Plateau Pass.
room.whispering_woods.5.desc: The forest rises into a vaulted canopy, green light filtering down in broken shafts. From here the woods feel less like a path and more like a place with its own weather, its own breath, and its own patience.
room.whispering_woods.6.desc: The forest opens slightly and the eastern valley is visible through gaps in the canopy. Gerlyas lies to the east — the village is close enough to smell the cook fires on still evenings. The path continues south into the deeper forest toward the mountain terrain where the pass system begins.
room.whispering_woods.7.desc: A quieter western reach of the woods where branches interlace overhead and the ground softens under old needles and leaf mold. Sound carries strangely here, arriving from directions that do not match the wind.
room.whispering_woods.8.desc: The forest dips into a sheltered grove where fallen trunks lie half-swallowed by moss. The air is cool and still, and the trees seem to lean inward as if listening.
room.mountain_pass.1.desc: Just outside Hydea's western gate, the Plateau Pass begins its descent south toward Xarra. The fortifications of the gate tower overhead; below, the mountain road drops away into the first switchbacks. This is the formal start of the Plateau Pass — the military road that connects Hydea to the canyon city. A guard post checks travellers in both directions.
room.mountain_pass.2.desc: The Plateau Pass descends from Hydea's southern gate into the first switchbacks of the mountain road. The city walls are still visible above as the path drops away. Cut stone and drainage channels — this road was built to last. Snow lingers in the northern shadows well into spring.
room.mountain_pass.3.desc: The pass road continues south through open mountain terrain. The Breswelc valley runs below to the east; ahead, the Xaryre range rises in successive ridges. The wind is constant and cold. Stone distance markers in old Myriac script stand at regular intervals along the road.
room.mountain_pass.4.desc: The Plateau Pass descends through a long section of switchbacks after the upper road levels off. The mountain slope falls steeply to the east; to the west, a ridge blocks the view of the lowlands. The road here is the most exposed section of the entire pass — wind and weather hit without shelter. The engineers who cut this road built low stone windbreaks along the western edge.
room.mountain_pass.5.desc: A long straight section of the Plateau Pass where the terrain levels between two ridges. In both directions the road is visible for an unusual distance — rare on a mountain road. Wind-carved rock formations flank the way. The altitude is enough to make exertion feel slightly harder. The next section begins climbing again toward the high point.
room.mountain_pass.6.desc: The Plateau Pass climbs toward its highest point before the canyon descent. Wind scours the exposed stone road. Looking north, Hydea is small against the mountain range behind it; looking south, the terrain begins to hint at the canyon geography ahead. The path levels briefly before the final descent.
room.mountain_pass.7.desc: The road narrows along a ledge carved straight into the mountain face. Wind scrapes across the stone without pause, and loose grit skitters over the edge before vanishing into the drop below.
room.mountain_pass.8.desc: A cracked distance marker stands beside the road, its old Myriac lettering worn almost smooth. The pass bends here around fractured rock, and the route ahead feels older than the roadwork that keeps it open.
room.mountain_pass.9.desc: The Plateau Pass turns west here and enters the upper canyon approach. The walls of the Xaryre close in on both sides. Ahead, the gap between Tresa and Roruk begins to come into view — the same canyon opening that from the plateau looks impossibly narrow. The stone underfoot changes from cut mountain road to ancient canyon floor.
room.mountain_pass.10.desc: A junction in the mountain road where the eastern valley path meets the Plateau Pass. North, the road climbs back toward Hydea. West, the pass begins its descent into the canyon approach toward Xarra. East, a path descends toward Gerlyas and the southern eastern valley. An old Myriac stone post marks the junction — its inscription nearly worn away, but the four-direction carving at its base is still clear.
room.mountain_pass.11.desc: The path from Gerlyas joins the Plateau Pass approach from the east. The terrain here is rocky and exposed; the Xaryre has its own weather in this southern section, different from the valley above. The Plateau Pass is audible before it is visible — wind through the canyon system creates a low, persistent sound that carries further than it should.
room.mountain_pass.13.desc: The road descends toward the Gerlyas side of the range. Stone gives way to thinner soil and stubborn grass, and the mountain wind carries the faint scent of woodsmoke from the valley below.
room.mountain_pass.14.desc: The canyon narrows to its final approach and the view of Xarra stops you in place. The city fills the gap between two enormous peaks — Tresa to the west, Roruk to the east. Stone terraces climb both canyon walls as far as the eye can follow. The oldest structures near the canyon floor show stonework no human mason could have cut — the foundations that dragons and the first peoples shaped together, three thousand years ago.
room.xarra.north.desc: The northern gate of Xarra is built directly into the canyon wall — the arch has no keystone because the stone around it was not assembled but shaped. Dragon-craft, the old name says, though most who pass through don't look up. The gate ward keeps a record of who enters and exits; everyone coming down from the pass is noted.
room.xarra.smithy.desc: The smithy district sits in an alcove off the northern terrace, sheltered from the wind by the canyon wall. The forges here run on coal brought up from the Breswelc river valley. The Xaryre iron they work is harder than lowland ore — Taro Vaeres in Royas learned his craft from a master who trained here.
room.xarra.academy.desc: The Academy of Xarra is the oldest school of magical and martial arts in Lura. The founding inscription above the entrance reads, in Myriac: 'What we build together endures.' The curriculum includes techniques developed in collaboration with dragons before the First Wars began — methods taught nowhere else in the kingdom.
room.xarra.manufactory.desc: The production quarter handles the practical work that keeps Xarra running — ore processing, weapon finishing, armor repair, food stores. The workers here move quickly and talk little. Everyone in this district knows how many days of supply the city has; it is not a comfortable number.
room.xarra.west.desc: The western terrace clings to the Tresa side of Xarra, its streets cut into old stone and linked by short, steep stairs. From here the city feels layered rather than built, each generation resting on the one below.
room.xarra.spellbound.desc: Spellbound Street is the oldest continuously occupied street in Lura — the scribes and enchanters here can trace their professional lineage back to the city's founding covenant. The shop fronts are narrow but deep, packed with scrolls, reagents, and tools. Above the doors, small carvings of dragon forms mark shops that carry stock the academies cannot legally sell elsewhere.
room.xarra.center.desc: The administrative heart of the city, where the canyon floor is at its widest. The Guild Hall occupies the largest building, its walls carved with the names of the founding compact between dragon-kind and the peoples of the Xaryre. The inscriptions are in old Myriac that few can read today — but everyone knows what they mean.
room.xarra.market.desc: The main market runs along the third terrace where the canyon widens enough to hold several hundred people at once. Traders from the lowlands mix with mountain suppliers. On clear days the sky between Tresa and Roruk is a narrow strip of blue directly overhead — bright, and impossibly far up.
room.xarra.cathedral.desc: The cathedral was not built by human hands alone — the vaulted ceiling shows the characteristic smooth curves of dragon-craft stonework, impossible to replicate with chisel and hammer alone. The healers who work here are the best in Lura, trained in methods that predate Tyriovan medicine by centuries.
room.xarra.west_gate.desc: The western gate faces the older roads out of Xarra. Its arch is narrower than the northern gate but deeper, with grooves in the threshold from centuries of cart wheels, patrol boots, and ceremonial processions.
room.xarra.south.desc: The southern district climbs the lower slopes of the Roruk flank in dense, steep neighborhoods — narrow stairs connecting terrace to terrace, the stone smoothed by generations of foot traffic. The Cathedral tower is visible from every alley. This is where most of Xarra's permanent residents actually live.
room.xarra.east.desc: The eastern district faces the Roruk peak and catches shade for most of the afternoon. Despite that, it is one of the more prosperous parts of the city — the clergy compound and several academic buildings occupy the choice spots near the canyon floor, close to the Cathedral.
room.xarra.eastern_gate.desc: The eastern gate stands closed. From beyond it, the sounds of conflict drift in — distant, but close enough that you can pick out individual shouts. A guard captain stands at the inner portcullis and does not look happy to see visitors coming this way.
room.xarra.palace.desc: The palace occupies the widest point of the Tresa flank — a compound of interlocking courts and halls that grew over three thousand years from the original covenant-hall where dragon and human leaders first met as equals. The garden between the outer walls and the main hall is famous: plants from every region of Lura, kept alive through winters that would kill them anywhere else.
room.hollow_crypt.1.desc: A passage that is clearly not mining work — the stone here was cut with precision that modern tools cannot match, following angles and curves that suggest intention rather than extraction. The sound of something mechanical in the distance; pressure on old metal.
room.hollow_crypt.2.desc: A round room that rises to a dome. No natural light — but the room is not dark. Faint bioluminescent growth covers the dome in patterns too regular to be accidental. Whatever faith was practiced here predates any record in Xarra's archives.
room.hollow_crypt.3.desc: Alcoves line the eastern wall — originally housing something that was removed long before this place was found. The stonework is consistent with the highest-quality Myriac construction: old-kingdom period, before the First Dragon Wars. Someone of means and patience built this.
room.hollow_crypt.4.desc: The passage divides through a gallery of shallow alcoves, many of them empty and some deliberately sealed. The stone here is colder than the rooms before it, and every footstep returns a fraction too late.
room.hollow_crypt.5.desc: The western counterpart to the eastern chamber. The alcoves here are still occupied — not by their original contents, but by whatever moved in during the long silence. The stonework is more refined than the eastern side; if there was a hierarchy in this place, it belonged here.
room.hollow_crypt.6.desc: A narrow reliquary runs along the northern side of the crypt. Most of its shelves are bare, but dust outlines what once rested there: small objects, carefully arranged, removed by hands that knew their worth.
room.hollow_crypt.7.desc: A straight span of worked stone connects the deeper chambers. The air is unnaturally still here, and even the usual drip of water seems absent, as if the crypt is holding its breath.
room.hollow_crypt.8.desc: The chamber before the deepest hollow is marked by red mineral veins running through the walls like old wounds. The floor slopes almost imperceptibly downward, guiding every path toward the dark beyond.
room.hollow_crypt.9.desc: A vast atrium with two rows of pillars carrying a vaulted ceiling that shouldn't stand by the engineering principles of the last eight hundred years. At the far end, a massive altar faces a stone figure so large it is difficult to understand as a single carved object — the proportions are not human.
room.royas.main.desc: Royas is barely a village — a dozen permanent households and the forge that defines it. The smoke from Taro Vaeres's smithy is the first thing you smell coming down the Nuvmito. A few villagers go about their day with the unhurried pace of people who have lived their whole lives between the same two peaks. The feeling here is different from anywhere else in Lura: something old, something alive, still present.
